newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Russian premier will work doubly hard for Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Russian premier will work doubly hard for Yeltsin.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Tuesday he was trying to convince ailing President Boris Yeltsin to pay more attention to his health and worry less about the affairs of state.

Chernomyrdin, designated to stand in for Yeltsin when the Russian leader undergoes a heart operation in the coming weeks, also told reporters he would work doubly hard when he became acting president.
"I will do everything in my power to be a worthy standin for the President," Chernomyrdin said in brief remarks after a meeting in Geneva with Swiss Foreign Minister Flavoi Cotti.
"I will have double the work to do -- for myself and for the President. That is my duty and I will do it with pleasure."
Chernomyrdin, on a 24-hour visit largely aimed at promoting the bid of St Petersburg for the 2004 Olympic Games, said that for the moment Yeltsin was still involving himself in running the country.
"We are discussing things together and I am trying to ensure that the President does not get too worried and that he pays more attention to his own health," the Russian prime minister declared.
When the operation takes place, he added, "we will do everything possible to ensure that the absence of Boris Yeltsin is not felt unduly."
Asked about plans for the expansion of the NATO alliance to take in states like Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic which were in the old Soviet orbit, Chernomyrdin said:

"We are against NATO's expansion to the East. We think there is no need for any hurry in this, and that we should all get to know each other better first and learn to work together. That is our firm position and we will not change it."

Chernomyrdin is due to have talks on Wednesday with Jean- Pascal Delamuraz, current holder of Switzerland's rotating presidency, and then meet International Olympic Committee (IOC) chief Juan-Antonio Samaranch in Lausanne.
The Russian Prime Minister heads the committee leading the bid of St Petersburg, the country's second city, for the Games in eight years time. The Olympics were staged in Moscow in 1980.
